channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Trump officials scrutinized Rep. Ilhan Omar in 2019. They didn’t find citizenship issues.
item.description: The earlier review of Omar’s immigration records looked at many of the same issues being investigated now. That review found no issue with her naturalization, an official familiar with the earlier effort said.

item.title: Three children and an adult killed in shooting at Oregon elementary school, authorities say
item.description: Police in Bend said the shooter is dead but that they “don’t have confirmation who shot the suspect.” Officials cautioned that the information was preliminary and could change.

item.title: Multiple people, including children, injured in shooting at an Oregon elementary school
item.description: Police in Bend said that the shooter is dead but that they “don’t have confirmation who shot the suspect.”

item.title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia appears to confirm she didn’t pass the bar
item.description: The acknowledgment to a right-wing media outlet comes after days of uncertainty about the legal credentials of the newly appointed spokeswoman for President Donald Trump.

item.title: Three weeks out, Trump’s election meddling lies mostly in ruins

item.title: Justice Department sues California officials over 20,000 alleged noncitizen voters
item.description: The Department of Justice sued the top election officials in California and Los Angeles County, claiming they were planning to count ballots from more than 20,000 alleged noncitizens in next month’s midterm elections.

item.title: Lawsuit alleges jail repeatedly served inmates food containing mice and insects
item.description: The plaintiffs in a class-action lawsuit say D.C.’s jail knew it was feeding them vermin and didn’t do enough to fix the problem.

item.title: It was meant to stop surprise medical bills. It cost Americans $17 billion instead.
item.description: If Congress wants to fix this problem in health care, it should reform the No Surprises Act.

item.title: Trump cancels Hegseth’s plan to live-stream Fort Hood shooter’s execution
item.description: President Donald Trump rejected Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan to live-stream the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, a former U.S. Army psychiatrist who killed numerous colleagues at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009.

item.title: Secret documents obtained by The Post reveal major donors behind $330 million for Trump’s ballroom
item.description: Tech giants Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million, the top contribution amount, the documents show. Absent from the list is President Donald Trump himself, who has said that he is helping to pay for the project.

item.title: The cover letter used to be a cornerstone of every job application. Not anymore.
item.description: Many job seekers are relying on AI to help with their applications. When anyone can submit a phenomenal cover letter, what's the point?

item.title: Trump’s rally schedule reveals more than any poll
item.description: Three weeks from Election Day, the president is spending his scarcest resource in red territory.

item.title: Rep. Nancy Mace accused these men of abuse. Now they face criminal charges.
item.description: South Carolina authorities said Wednesday they arrested three men whom Mace, in a speech in the U.S. House, had accused of wrongdoing.

item.title: The biggest mistake that people with knee pain make, according to an orthopedic surgeon
item.description: Surgeon Howard Luks has built his practice around the idea that our joints can remain strong and functional throughout life, with some basic care and feeding.

item.title: An SNL host seemed shocked by women’s fitness attire. Nobody tell him about the ’80s, Ashley Fetters Maloy writes in a column.
item.description: Skimpy, stretchy gym outfits have been around longer than comedian Shane Gillis has been alive.

item.title: The 40 best restaurants in the D.C. area
item.description: Our food critic’s favorite restaurants of the year showcase the culinary abundance of the region.

item.title: Reflecting Pool liner failed in 85 places due to flawed renovation, inspection found
item.description: The damage identified during an inspection commissioned by the contractor is far more extensive than has been previously reported, a document obtained by The Post shows.

item.title: How Donald Trump, agent of chaos, lost control
item.description: The president should be far more attuned to why his party is likely to suffer an electoral rout.

item.title: Social Security paychecks will go up by about $75 a month in January
item.description: The bump in benefits reflects a 3.6 percent cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) increase, the biggest since 2023, when inflation ran historically hot in the aftermath of the pandemic.

item.title: Prices increased faster in September in last inflation report before Election Day
item.description: Inflation rose to a 3.7 percent annual pace, more than expected.

item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Judge extends White House access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico while lawsuit over media ban proceeds
item.description: U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a preliminary injunction late Tuesday, supplanting a temporary restraining order he granted Sept. 24. The move allows the outlets to maintain regular access to White House grounds while litigation continues. President Donald Trump last month barred the organizations from the White House for reporting what he called “fake news.”

item.title: Investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar focuses on her birth date and decades-old immigration paperwork, people familiar said
item.description: The Minnesota Democrat, who was born in Somalia and fled civil war there with her family before immigrating to the United States in 1995, has repeatedly rejected allegations that her documents used to secure legal status and U.S. citizenship contained falsehoods. Such claims have circulated in conservative media for years, and she dismissed them again this week as “baseless lies and smear campaigns.”

item.title: Sens. Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Jon Ossoff (D-Georgia) face their challengers in debates tonight. Follow our coverage.
item.description: Senate candidates in three critical competitive states are gathering for debates Tuesday night. We’ll cover the one-hour Maine and Georgia debates live, and we’ll also monitor the Iowa debate between Rep. Ashley Hinson (R) and state Rep. Josh Turek (D) later in the evening.

item.title: What’s the best way to reheat pizza? We tried 5 popular methods.
item.description: The best method, of course, is not always the fastest one.

item.title: OpenAI employee arrested by FBI after “sophisticated” recording device was found in an executive conference room
item.description: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old citizen of Saudi Arabia who has been working at OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested Oct. 9 and appeared in federal court Tuesday. OpenAI is one of a handful of companies at the cutting edge of developing highly capable artificial intelligence models.

item.title: Pope Leo’s surgery removed cancerous lung nodule, Vatican says
item.description: The 71-year-old underwent an operation to remove a pulmonary adenocarcinoma, among the most common types of lung cancer. Officials said it was “successfully completed.” The diagnosis raised alarm over the pope’s health only 17 months into his papacy.

item.title: These bad candidates could cost either party the Senate
item.description: The midterms will be a test: Is partisanship so strong that even defective candidates can win?

item.title: White House scrambles over questions on new press secretary’s background
item.description: President Donald Trump said Katie Zacharia is an “attorney,” but her bar credentials are unclear.

item.title: Cornell bans fraternity houses from hosting parties for remainder of school year as rape investigation continues
item.description: The university’s president, who announced the ban, cited women’s safety concerns following allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a fraternity house.

item.title: Why you should make your phone worse on purpose, according to our columnist Michael J. Coren
item.description: If you’re stressed out by your phone, these evidence-backed methods can help you regain control.

item.title: Wife of House Speaker Mike Johnson gets paid to minister to Hill staffers, but nonprofit’s funding is a mystery
item.description: Kelly Johnson’s faith-based counseling services are the centerpiece of an organization that does not disclose its donors.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Lift social media ban on mother-in-law for family peace?
item.description: Mother-in-law uses socials as a passive-aggressive “burn book.” Letter writer asks whether dropping her is unsupportive of spouse.

item.title: Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle has been asked to resign, new White House press secretary says
item.description: Guilfoyle, the ambassador to Greece, has faced allegations she asked a political donor for $100,000 to pay her personal American Express bill. She has denied any wrongdoing.

item.title: U.K. intelligence chief warns Iran is shifting toward ‘harder targets,’ citing suspected plot against air base used by U.S. bombers
item.description: In an annual speech on threats, Ken McCallum, the head of MI5, said there was a “major shift” in Tehran’s ambitions to attack military sites and other high-security targets.

item.description: Trump’s diesel-deal feud with Zelensky obscures a more important effort, David Ignatius writes.

item.title: Trump’s midterm road show reveals GOP troubles — and his own priorities
item.description: Republicans need the president to mobilize voters, but his low approval ratings limit where he can help.

item.title: How to take care of your knees in your 20s, 30s, 40s and beyond
item.description: The latest science suggests knees are more resilient than you think.

item.title: They came to Washington to dismantle government. Now, they’re profiting from it.
item.description: DOGE alumni have leveraged their government experience, raising at least half a billion dollars for firms spanning cyberwarfare, AI and data centers, a Post analysis found.

item.title: ‘You did your absolute worst’: Judge criticizes Trump administration after it removed hundreds of trees at D.C. golf course
item.description: U.S. District Judge Ana C. Reyes scolded the government for ignoring her repeated warnings to give notice before work continued on the historic public course President Donald Trump has proposed overhauling.

item.title: Rep. Ilhan Omar calls search at D.C. home part of a Trump intimidation campaign
item.description: The search appears to be the type of action that law enforcement officials have typically avoided so close to an election in the past. The Minnesota Democrat is up for reelection.

item.title: Trump administration blew past judge-imposed deadline to halt running taxpayer-funded campaign-style ads
item.description: A federal judge issued a temporary order Sunday blocking the ads from airing, but two of the ads ran into the early hours of Monday, advertising data from AdImpact shows.

item.title: Sixth person who had measles has died in Pennsylvania, local coroner says
item.description: The state is in the midst of a growing outbreak as the United States faces the highest measles tally since 1991.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Mom delivers final blow after a lifetime of disappointments
item.description: Mom, who barely conceals her motherhood regrets, just withdrew the one form of care she’d been willing to give the letter writer.

item.title: No wonder the government can’t off-load this building. Look inside.
item.description: HUD’s former headquarters is a financial sinkhole that illustrates a larger problem.

item.title: He reached the Americas centuries before Columbus. Why doesn’t he get more credit?
item.description: Led by Leif Erikson, the Vikings arrived in the year 1000, give or take a decade — half a millennium before a certain other European explorer first landed in the Bahamas.

item.title: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home in D.C.
item.description: Last month, U.S. officials said federal authorities were investigating whether the Somali American lawmaker unlawfully entered the country by falsifying her immigration paperwork. The Justice Department did not confirm what investigation Monday’s search was connected to.
